text:
alisa: seeing a spike in warm-pool failures and long node init times in ap-northeast-1 for the last ~10m. GPU nodes stuck at `waiting for keystore` and bootlooping. link: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/cluster/provisioning?orgId=1

pete: yup, observed. warm-pool healthy count dropped from 120 -> 42. provision queue backed up, latency for init-step `fetch-keystore-token` went 200ms -> 3s.

dmitri: keystore-proxy-2 logs show repeated 500s, and audit-shipper backlog grew. sample:```
2025-06-02T09:02:11Z keystore-proxy-2 ERROR fetchToken failed status=500 body="audit-write-timeout"
```

keystore-bot: ALERT: keystore-proxy-2 5xx rate 45% (5m), audit-shipper-latency P99=8s, queue_length=13k :rotating_light:

karen: anything changed on VPC / privatelink rules? we recently tightened ingress to privatelink-tunnel for egress audit. could be backpressure.

alisa: yes we rolled firewall change at 08:55 that added restrictive TCP windowing on privatelink endpoints (reason: reduce noisy long connections). suspecting it causes head-of-line on the audit stream which keystore stalls on.

pete: also noticed NAT gateway SNAT port exhaustion intermittently when audit retries spike. NAT metrics show connection rate +3x. that will add extra latency for the token fetch path.

dmitri: repro command showing 503:```
curl -v https://keystore-proxy.internal/v1/token -H "Authorization: Bearer svc-ops"
* Connection #0 to host keystore-proxy.internal left intact
< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< Retry-After: 2
{ "error": "audit-backlog" }
```

pete: rolling the privatelink firewall rule back now (rule id fw-priv-892). will monitor.

deploy-bot: rollback fw-priv-892 initiated by pete @ 2025-06-02T09:14:03Z. status: in-progress.

alisa: note for postmortem: this interaction spans network (privatelink windowing), keystore audit pipeline, and NAT port pressure on the same egress path — caused cascading token fetch failures -> GPU nodes stuck waiting -> provisioning queue growth -> cost + degraded SLA.

karen: quick ask: can we throttle audit shipper at source to shed non-critical events until backlog drains? that would stop the head-of-line.

dmitri: agree. adding soft-drop for debug-level events + batching up to 200ms. will push a config to keystore-proxy canary.

ops-runbook: runbook step executed: disable fw-priv-892 OR increase privatelink TCP window to 512k. recommended temporary mitigation: rollback firewall + enable audit soft-drop.

pete: fw rollback complete. keystore-proxy 5xx rate ↓ to 6% in 60s. audit-shipper backlog decreasing. warm-pool healthy count recovering.

keystore-bot: RECOVERY: keystore-proxy-2 5xx rate back to baseline 4% (5m). audit-shipper-latency P99=320ms.

dmitri: rough cost impact calc while queue was backed up: provisioning retries + extra NAT egress => ~+$3.8k/day if sustained. not a full month, but noticeable on committed GPU spend.

alisa: creating a short postmortem and P0 action items: 1) add e2e test for privatelink windowing vs audit stream, 2) implement audit soft-drop + backpressure signal for keystore->auditor, 3) update network change CA checklist to include warm-pool/keystore impact.

karen: added to my calendar for tomorrow: incident review 10:30 PST.

pete: marking this thread resolved for now. reopen if anything spikes. :thumbsup:
